headline: Amazon Web Services' chief executive said the company should speak up more about the everyday services data centres provide, as public opposition to them grows.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 1: the interview was already carried in our 10 Oct 2026 edition and Business Insider's piece is dated 10 Oct, before today's window; only the data-centre messaging remarks are new.
importance_line: A cloud chief answering data-centre opposition bears first on communities deciding whether to host new data centres, then on local officials and AI companies seeking permits; it is the company's own pitch to the public, and the tax example is an illustration with no independent evidence.
summary: Business Insider reports, as carried by Yahoo Finance, that Matt Garman, chief executive of Amazon's cloud arm AWS, said on the A16z Show podcast that the company needs to be "more vocal and be more upfront" about the benefits of data centres, arguing that a community asked whether it still wants Netflix, which says it runs "the vast majority" of its computing on AWS, will say yes, and that residents might see the buildings differently if told their tax bill was "$5,000 less" than it would otherwise be, an illustration rather than a measured figure. It comes as a Fox News survey last month found 71 percent of registered voters oppose building an AI data centre in their area, and from the same interview our 10 Oct 2026 edition carried Garman's remark that he is not worried about an AI spending bubble.
notes: Benzinga's page (the pool item) is blocked (403); read Business Insider's story by Brent D. Griffiths on Yahoo Finance and BigGo Finance's summary; the url is the Yahoo page. Same podcast interview as our 10 Oct 2026 edition's Garman entry; new today are his remarks on community opposition.
